what: The cells of the suite above that another package's index cites. A SEAM BETWEEN TWO PACKAGES, and a data file rather than a list inside either suite because neither package should be scraping structure out of the other's source.
readBy: implementations/runtime/smoke/run-driver.smoke.ts -- asserts every sentence here is a cell THAT RUN EXECUTED, exactly once. That is the half source text cannot answer: `c` is silent on success, so a cell commented out or left dead behind a condition keeps its sentence in the file while the claim stops being made.

packages/lang/smoke/differential.smoke.ts -- asserts SET EQUALITY, both directions, between its version-split matrix's driver rows and this list. Containment either way alone leaves a hole, and the direction the runtime suite cannot see is a row added to that matrix whose sentence never reached this file.
why: MEASURED, on both sides independently: with one cited cell commented out, a source-text
containment check still passes -- grep finds the sentence TWICE, because the commented-out line
still carries it -- and the language package's index printed `every one resolved by name` about a
cell that no longer ran. Neither cell above can be satisfied by a quotation.
OWNED BY THE RUNTIME PACKAGE, because these are its cells' names and it is the package that renames
them. A rename lands here in the same commit or the suite that owns the rename reds first.
cells: a record no engine here serves is RELEASED, not failed and not thrown
and it is refused by name, L5023
and the refusal names both the version it met and the set this build serves
and the run was not touched: the refusal came before the activation, so only the first holder's is there
a record that names no language version at all is refused the same way
and the refusal says the record names none, rather than interpolating the missing value
a record at the version the ENGINE writes is released by the dispatcher, L5023, naming it
while the same spec at a version this build DOES serve gets past the table
a fresh run completes on the engine this build serves
and it is stamped with the version of the ENGINE that ran it, not with the current language
